name: MC3D conventional-superconductivity screening and Eliashberg dataset
description: Electron–phonon and superconductivity calculations on experimental-derived MC3D metal structures, with refined isotropic and anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg subsets.
count_display: 4,533 nonmagnetic metals screened; refined subsets of 250 isotropic and 140 anisotropic Eliashberg calculations
count_scope: Version 4 initial Allen–Dynes screening cohort; refined subsets are nested

sources.title: Charting the landscape of Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer superconductors in experimentally known compounds — version 4
sources.evidence: Archive describes 4,533 initial metals, 250 refined dynamically stable structures and 140 anisotropic cases; supplies AiiDA archives and tables.

sources.title: Materials Cloud version 4 metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms publication date 2025-11-04 and CC BY 4.0 deposit rights.

caveats: Tc labels are calculated; experimental provenance of the starting crystal structures does not make Tc experimental.
The 250 and 140 cases are subsets, not additional structures to add to 4,533.
Earlier preprint/archive versions quote smaller refined subsets; these counts refer specifically to version 4.
Overlaps the broad MC3D structural family; count this as a property release, not an independent sum of new structures.

additional_counts.scope: Version 4 refined dynamically stable isotropic Migdal–Eliashberg subset
Version 4 anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg subset of the refined cohort

name: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
description: High-throughput electron–phonon training data and follow-up calculations used to screen conventional superconductors.
count_scope: Initial computed training dataset described in the 2023 archive; unique-material count not independently recounted

sources.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds — data archive
sources.evidence: Author deposit describes around 7,000 electron–phonon calculations used to train a model, followed by screening approximately 200,000 compounds and DFPT validation of selected candidates.

sources.title: Materials Cloud 2023.163 metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms 2023-10-30 release and CC BY 4.0 deposit rights.

caveats: Approximately 200,000 screened compounds carry model predictions and must not be counted as 200,000 DFPT-labeled superconductors.
The ranked count is approximate and denotes calculation cases; an independent exact unique-structure recount was not performed.
Computed Tc and stability screening do not establish experimental superconductivity.
Training data can overlap other published high-throughput electron–phonon collections; no cross-family deduplication was performed.

name: Antiperovskite superconductivity DFPT dataset
description: Electron–phonon calculations for cubic antiperovskites XYZ3 with metal X/Z and H, B, C, N, O or P on the Y site.
count_scope: Starting DFPT cohort in the 2022 archive, including dynamically unstable cases

sources.title: Superconductivity in antiperovskites — data archive
sources.evidence: Describes 384 starting DFPT cases, approximately 40% with imaginary phonons, and 16 calculated cases above 5 K.

sources.title: Materials Cloud 2022.49 metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms 2022-04-06 release, downloadable calculation archives and CC BY 4.0 rights.

caveats: The cohort includes dynamically unstable materials; 384 is not a count of stable superconductors.
The further 44 materials above 5 K are model predictions and are not added to the DFPT cohort count.
All superconducting temperatures in this release are theoretical.

additional_counts.scope: Initial DFPT cohort with calculated Tc above 5 K

name: Superhydra binary-hydride database
description: Template-generated binary hydrides with calculated electronic, vibrational and chemical descriptors at high pressure.
version: 2023 Physical Review Materials release; 2022 preprint dataset
count_display: 880 hypothetical structures; 139 superconducting cases in the McMillan–Allen–Dynes approximation
count_scope: Binary-hydride template cohort at 200 GPa, not 880 independent Tc-positive observations

sources.title: Mapping Superconductivity in High-Pressure Hydrides: The Superhydra Project
sources.evidence: Authors report 880 hypothetical binary-hydride structures and 139 superconducting cases under the McMillan–Allen–Dynes approximation.

sources.title: Superhydra Physical Review Materials article and Supplemental Material
sources.evidence: Published article identifies the supplemental CSV release; the cohort is generated by element substitution into structural templates.

caveats: The main count includes the full hypothetical-structure cohort, not just calculated superconductors.
Structure-linked classification is conservative: complete atomic coordinates in the supplemental CSV were not independently audited.
Dataset-specific reuse license was not verified.
The campaign is pressure-specific and calculated; it does not establish synthesis, experimental Tc or ambient-pressure stability.

additional_counts.scope: McMillan–Allen–Dynes superconducting subset of the 880-case cohort

name: JARVIS high-pressure hydride superconductivity campaign
description: Pressure-resolved DFT/DFPT hydride calculations, superconductivity labels and accompanying ALIGNN models released by the authors.
count_display: Over 900 high-pressure hydride electron–phonon/DFT calculation cases
count_scope: Author paper v4 calculation campaign; repeated pressures per candidate are not unique compounds

sources.title: Data-driven Design of High Pressure Hydride Superconductors using DFT and Deep Learning — author version 4
sources.evidence: Latest author version describes over 900 EPC/DFT cases spanning multiple pressures and 122 dynamically stable cases above the MgB2 reference Tc.

sources.title: High-pressure hydride dataset Figshare metadata
sources.evidence: Version 1 deposit contains raw DFT hydride data, ALIGNN data/models, a notebook and phase energies; license is CC BY 4.0.

caveats: The same candidate is evaluated at multiple pressures; over 900 is not a unique-composition count.
This pressure-resolved release is distinct from the existing JARVIS ambient 3D and 2D superconductivity cohorts, but source structures overlap JARVIS, 3DSC and earlier hydride work.
Calculated Tc labels and model predictions coexist in the package; model predictions are not additional DFT validation.
Earlier manuscript versions used different training-set wording; the selected lower-bound count follows author version 4.

additional_counts.scope: Dynamically stable computed cases reported above MgB2 reference Tc of 39 K

name: HTSC-2025 ambient-pressure BCS superconductor benchmark
description: A curated benchmark of crystal CIFs and literature theoretical Tc values for recent ambient-pressure conventional-superconductor candidates.
version: ScienceDB V1; official Hugging Face JSON snapshot 2026-11-01
count_display: 140 material records with CIF structures and Tc values
count_scope: 140 top-level material keys independently counted in official HTSC-2025.json

sources.title: HTSC-2025 official dataset card
sources.evidence: Describes 140 ambient-pressure BCS materials compiled from recent theoretical studies, grouped into six material families.

sources.title: HTSC-2025 official JSON data
sources.evidence: Independently parsed 140 material keys; entries contain CIF text and a tc field. SHA-256 fba2681d115fcd131e0e09086bf0a271d6ecb5ef9e46f238be98d3faac0f92a3.

sources.title: ScienceDB HTSC-2025 V1 DOI metadata
sources.evidence: Registrant metadata gives version V1, MIT rights and the theoretical-superconductor benchmark description.

caveats: The cohort primarily compiles predicted superconductors, not 140 experimentally demonstrated high-Tc materials; MgB2 also appears as a reference.
The dataset viewer can display one row because the JSON is a single dictionary; 140 is the number of material entries inside it.
Literature-calculated Tc values can use different computational assumptions and should not be treated as a uniformly recomputed experimental benchmark.

name: SuperCon² text-extracted superconductivity records
description: Automatically extracted literature records linking material mentions to critical-temperature statements, pressure and bibliographic context.
count_display: 18,943 nonheader rows in the named cleaned CSV; original v22.12.03 has 40,324 rows
count_scope: Named v23.04.28 cleaned CSV, independently recounted; rows are not necessarily unique materials

sources.title: SuperCon² author repository
sources.evidence: Repository describes automatic superconductivity information extraction from an arXiv-paper corpus and exposes versioned CSV outputs.

sources.title: SuperCon² cleaned CSV v23.04.28
sources.evidence: CSV parser counted 18,943 nonheader rows; SHA-256 f7598571a59a35ae1ba281643f41f80248863f9e73e13b39e45659ea6170eb2d.

sources.title: SuperCon² original CSV v22.12.03
sources.evidence: Original version independently contains 40,324 nonheader rows; it is not interchangeable with the later cleaned release.

caveats: Rows are extracted assertions and can include repeated mentions, incomplete formulas, and statements about experimental or theoretical work.
These counts do not establish unique superconducting materials or independently validated experimental Tc labels.
Data-specific reuse license was not verified; software or article licensing is not substituted for dataset rights.
Shares literature and extraction methodology with SuperMat; no union deduplication was performed.

additional_counts.scope: Original supercon2_v22.12.03.csv, independently counted; not additive to cleaned release

name: SuperMat public superconductivity linked-record CSV
description: Public linked material, critical-temperature, pressure and measurement-method records exported from the SuperMat annotated literature corpus.
count_scope: Public CSV 2.0 export, independently counted; not the entire article-annotation corpus

sources.title: SuperMat author repository README
sources.evidence: Specifies dataset CC BY 4.0 and code Apache 2.0; notes copyrighted full-text corpus cannot be publicly distributed and is held in a private submodule.

sources.title: SuperMat public CSV 2.0
sources.evidence: Independently parsed 1,305 nonheader rows with material, tcValue, pressure, me_method and source-filename fields. SHA-256 80e84ab67649a562a838c5a58fa8bb8025fe1e3225ad2eb664d9bcf3be8ed3ce.

caveats: Public linked CSV is accessible; full copyrighted article text and full annotations are not generally public.
Rows describe literature relations and may include partial material mentions; they are not 1,305 unique compositions or independently measured Tc values.
Original paper corpus statistics describe another unit/version and are not substituted for this CSV row count.

name: SC-CoMIcs superconductivity information-extraction corpus
description: Superconductivity abstract corpus with stand-off named-entity and relation annotations for materials information extraction.
count_scope: SC-CoMIcs version 3 corpus; abstracts are not unique material records
license: CC BY-NC 3.0 (deposit and abstract text); separate annotation-specific license Not verified

sources.title: SC-CoMIcs Mendeley Data version 3
sources.evidence: Author deposit describes 1,000 abstracts and stand-off annotations; abstract sharing is specifically permitted under CC BY-NC 3.0 and version 3 does not change the corpus content.

sources.title: SC-CoMIcs author repository
sources.evidence: Provides corpus tools and annotated files; links abstract text to the Mendeley deposit under CC BY-NC 3.0.

caveats: Abstract text has a noncommercial license; a separate annotation-specific license was not independently verified.
The ranked count denotes documents, not superconducting compounds or measured Tc observations.
Useful for information-extraction benchmarks, not a ready-made atomic-structure/Tc dataset.

sources.title: JARVIS supercon_chem Figshare version 1 metadata
sources.evidence: Confirms 2023-05-20 deposit, CC BY 4.0 rights, the downloadable JSON ZIP, and provenance links to vstanev1/Supercon and the Stanev paper.

sources.title: Official supercon_chem JSON ZIP
sources.evidence: Independently parsed 16,414 records with id, Tc and formula fields. ZIP SHA-256 14b7489822a1c25407cd6c83989dfca7f14263dfe6b5dc9f859969430c09e5b7.

caveats: Contains no atomic coordinates; source identifiers and formulas do not establish an unambiguous crystal structure.

Official JARVIS DFT supercon_3d and supercon_2d cohorts have different structures, labels and counts.
